title: Segment-wide replay recovers both established terminal controls
claim: Within the declared six-operation family, the segment-wide runtime ranks the established Page 73 sequential-prime/totient operator and Page 74 direct-GP operator first; each known control exceeds all 500 retained full-family shuffles in both token and vocabulary measures.
why_it_matters: It demonstrates that the runtime can recognize known terminal plaintext when the correct operation is present, establishing a positive control before interpreting failures on unsolved material.
controls: Two established public terminal plaintexts and operators.
Exact JSON/CSV cross-check and empirical-p recomputation.
limitations: Both terminal plaintexts were already known.
Private typed event streams are not redistributed, so the public verifier audits the complete retained terminal ledger rather than transforming source glyphs.
Two successful controls do not establish an operation for unsolved segments.
does_not_claim: An HMS-originated translation of Page 73 or Page 74.
Any new LP2 plaintext, key, locator, endpoint, or solve.
That one of the six tested operations must decode every unsolved segment.
That the operation-selector field has been identified.
current_interpretation: Retain Page 73 and Page 74 as positive regression controls for the segment runtime; require separate preregistered evidence before promoting any unsolved-segment output.
